parallel.requirements: The parallel parent and children recognized the std-only Rust 2021 project requirement, root test1.rs deliverable, C atoi-style CLI behavior, exact trailing-space/no-newline formatting, and byte-for-byte reference matching for regular 3n-gon earcut output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept orchestration and verification ownership after a short probe, then delegated implementation to agent-0 and an independent differential harness/reference-probe task to agent-1. The split had clear non-overlapping output ownership: agent-0 wrote /output, agent-1 wrote /tmp/earcut_check.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 wrote a full Rust earcut port in /output/earcut.rs, a root /output/test1.rs entry file, and Cargo.toml, including linked-list triangulation, z-order hashing above 80 vertices, C atoi semantics, and exact output writing.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The implementation child wrote the final project files directly into /output, then the parent consumed the returned child summaries, ran the returned harness against /output/test1, checked larger n values, listed final files, and delivered the implemented project.
parallel.verification: Verification included the implementation child's rustc and Cargo builds, byte comparisons over representative n and CLI edge cases, the harness child's reference probes and 35-case script self-test, parent-run harness checks, parent large-n checks for n=5000 and n=100000, and the official 39/39 evaluator pass.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No required behavior remained visibly unfinished at closure. The child noted hole-handling code was unexercised, but the target program only creates a single convex ring, and all required generated-program tests passed.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same prompt requirements: Rust 2021, no external crates, std::env::args parsing, exact byte output, complete Cargo project, root test1.rs, and black-box inference from the provided executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run kept all work in one owner: it probed behavior, wrote project files, built, debugged failures, managed its own todo list, and reran verification without child handoffs or shared ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote Cargo.toml, src/cli.rs, src/earcut.rs, and test1.rs, fixed a Rust type-inference compile error, adjusted atoi overflow behavior, then replaced a linked-list sort implementation that caused a spatial-index hang at n=27.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because all code lived in one local trajectory, integration was direct: the root binary referenced the src modules, the direct rustc binary and Cargo release binary were rebuilt after fixes, and the final artifact set contained the expected files.
serial.verification: The serial run byte-compared n=0..150, selected larger values through n=5000, several CLI edge and integer-boundary cases, inspected output bytes for n=2, ran cargo test --release, and then passed the official 39/39 evaluator.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved task defect remained at closure. The temporary failed fmt command and spatial-index hang were corrected before final verification, while rustfmt itself was not installed in the environment.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one writer in /output and resolved all edits within that single trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared final workspace but without observable collision, overwrite, or provenance instability; serial avoided shared writes by using one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed within the agent and cell budgets, did not time out, and closed after final harness, large-n, and file-structure checks.

comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial consumed more wall-clock and token budget due to local debugging, but neither run closed under an adverse parallel coordination timeout or incomplete deliverable.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial passed 39 of 39. The difference is the route to the same correct deliverable. Parallel delegated implementation and harness construction to separate completed children, then the parent joined both results and ran whole-output comparisons. Serial did the same categories of work in one trajectory and spent extra local debugging on a compile error, atoi boundary behavior, and a spatial-index hang before reaching the same acceptance state.
parallel_contributors: Clear separation between implementation and independent harness creation produced a built binary and an external byte-comparison script before parent acceptance.
Parent consumed both child results and reran the harness plus large-n comparisons after the child implementation had been built.
serial_contributors: Single actor retained all context and corrected implementation defects through local reads, edits, rebuilds, and comparisons.
Final serial verification covered broad n ranges, CLI edge cases, output-byte inspection, cargo test, and official evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial initially had a Rust type-inference build failure and later a spatial-index hang, both corrected before closure.
Parallel's implementation child produced a working root-level earcut.rs/test1.rs layout, while serial used src/earcut.rs and src/cli.rs modules.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both completed official evaluations passed

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was explicit: the parent delegated the porting task to agent-0 and that child wrote the Rust implementation and entry files.
There were not multiple independently written implementation components requiring unowned reconciliation; the parent owned the final join and checks after child completion.
Assembly ownership was present because agent-0 wrote the package manifest, root test1.rs, and binary, and artifact validation later found the expected entry file and build outputs.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition from delegation through returned results, final harness execution, large-n checks, file inspection, and final response.
The parent performed a brief probe, then launched implementation and harness children; productive work was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight with an adverse delay consequence.

Investigation and implementation were not organized as a completed first phase followed by deadline-constrained implementation; the implementation child and harness child ran as separate productive scopes and both completed.
No indispensable implementation or verification path was starved; the implementation child completed and the parent still ran final verification before closure.
The parallel run used only two children, finished without timeout, and had completed child results plus post-join verification; breadth did not exhaust the finite budget.
Although agent-0 had the broad implementation assignment, it completed the implementation, builds, and byte checks, leaving no unfinished indispensable work from an overbroad child scope.

The implementation child was briefed to port the mapbox earcut task, create /output/test1.rs, compile, and report verification; the harness child was given explicit comparison cases and /output write restrictions. No child-produced work became unusable due to an omitted known requirement.

The separately owned scopes had a concrete interface: the implementation child produced /output/test1 and the harness child built a script that accepts the Rust binary path. The parent ran that script successfully against /output/test1.
No known finding or constraint disappeared between actors; both child summaries reached the parent, and the parent acted on their essential contents.
The returned summaries were substantial but decision-usable; the parent reduced them to final harness and large-n checks instead of leaving the information unconsumed.
The parent did not consume a superseded child report; it verified the current /output/test1 after both children had completed.
The two child returns were compatible: one reported a built implementation and the other reported a harness and reference findings. No incompatible reports remained unadjudicated.
The parent did not accept only on file existence or child say-so; it ran the comparison harness and large-n checks after joining child results before finalizing.
There was no replacement or retry child in the parallel trajectory; both initial children completed and their results were used.

candidates.reason: No parallel child was stopped or cancelled before returning a needed result; both child Agent calls returned completed summaries.
A complete candidate was not left unpromoted or unplaced; the implementation child built /output/test1 and the parent verified and finalized it before closure.
The parent ran verification only after both child results had returned; there is no observed later merge after the relevant integrated checks.
The delegated implementation was returned to the parent and used: the parent received agent-0's completed summary and ran tests against /output/test1.
The verifier/harness child returned concrete findings to the parent, and the parent then ran the script; no verifier result was trapped below the parent.
No required parallel child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; both completed normally, so there was no failed scope requiring takeover.
Completed child results were not ignored: the parent used the implementation result by testing /output/test1 and used the harness result by executing /tmp/earcut_check/compare.sh.
The parent did not wait until timeout or near deadline without inspection; it acted after child returns and the run completed with substantial provider budget remaining.
The only implementation owner wrote the final /output project; the other child wrote a /tmp harness and did not create a competing implementation path.
No two live parallel agents are observed editing the same source or configuration file; agent-0 owns /output files and agent-1 owns /tmp/earcut_check/compare.sh.
There is no observed replacement, deletion, recreation, or wholesale rewrite of a non-entry source file produced by another parallel actor.
No competing agent replaced the required executable or root test1.rs; agent-0 created them and the parent only executed and inspected them.
There is no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion by another actor that invalidated final-tree work or provenance; artifact validation found a coherent output tree.
The parallel run did not have multiple live implementation writers in /output causing unstable state or provenance trouble; the harness child explicitly stayed outside /output.
The harness script created by agent-1 was an intended verification deliverable, not an accidental contaminating fixture or reference input consumed as stable task state.
